method: Items are published only when an official primary source or at least two independent publishers support them.

items.headline: China congratulates Indonesia's new foreign minister Arrmanatha Nasir after cabinet reshuffle
items.summary: Arrmanatha Nasir, previously deputy foreign minister, was inaugurated as foreign minister on 1 October, replacing Sugiono, who moved to a coordinating ministry. On 8 October a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said Beijing wants to deepen cooperation with Jakarta.
items.note: Swearing-in took place on 1 October; the reporting used here is dated 3 and 8 October.

sources.title: China welcomes Arrmanatha Nasir as Indonesia's new foreign minister
sources.evidence: Foreign Minister Wang Yi has sent his congratulations to Indonesian Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir,

sources.title: A ministry restored
sources.evidence: handed the foreign affairs portfolio to Arrmanatha “Tata” Nasir

items.headline: Indonesia weighs moratorium on new plants making semi-processed nickel
items.summary: Coordinating Minister Bahlil Lahadalia said on 7 October that the government is discussing a moratorium on new facilities producing semi-processed nickel, citing oversupply and weak prices. The Jakarta Post reported he put the supply surplus at about 2.5 million tonnes. No decision has been announced.
topics: Critical raw materials and supply chains
items.note: Plan under discussion, not a decision. Surplus figure as reported by The Jakarta Post.

sources.evidence: Indonesia is discussing a plan to impose a moratorium on development of new nickel processing facilities

sources.evidence: We want to start choosing which industries should continue and which need a moratorium

items.headline: Pontianak court opens class action against Indonesian state over forest fires and haze
items.summary: A court in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, opened a class action on 7 October accusing the president and nine other officials of gross negligence over recurring fires. None of the defendants attended and judges adjourned the hearing to 21 October. Plaintiffs ask for a declaration of a national disaster.
items.note: Allegations are those of the plaintiffs. A similar suit in South Sumatra was dismissed last year, according to AFP.

sources.evidence: the government was negligent in failing to prevent and adequately deal with forest and land fires

sources.evidence: They did not show up.

items.headline: House of Representatives passes new Employment Protection Law
items.summary: Indonesia's House of Representatives passed the Employment Protection Bill into law on 6 October after all factions agreed. It has 23 chapters and 313 articles. The Jakarta Post reported that it replaces labour provisions of the Job Creation Law and that unions welcomed it, while the committee chair said the balance among stakeholders is not yet ideal.
items.note: Provisions as described by The Jakarta Post and unions; the final text had not been published at the time of reporting.

items.headline: Constitutional Court dismisses petition challenging Vice President Gibran's candidacy
items.summary: On 6 October the Constitutional Court unanimously dismissed a petition over Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's 2024 election, saying it could not disqualify him from office. Justices said no graduation certificate had been presented. The petitioners' lawyer said the ruling could give parliament grounds for impeachment.
items.note: The impeachment view is the petitioners' lawyer's; no impeachment process has been announced.

sources.evidence: All nine judges dismissed the petition

sources.evidence: neither disqualifies Gibran nor affects the office he currently holds

sources.title: Top court quashes petition to disqualify Gibran
sources.evidence: The court cannot disqualify Gibran from his position as vice president.

items.headline: Government says it will not clear forest areas for new rice fields
items.summary: At the Indonesia International Sustainability Forum on 6 October, climate and energy envoy Hashim Djojohadikusumo said the government sees no further need to expand rice cultivation into forest areas. The Forestry Ministry said it could not yet confirm that all existing activities in the affected regions will stop.
items.note: Scale of the earlier plan differs by outlet: about 2 million ha (The Jakarta Post), 3 million ha (AFP). Implementation timing is unclear.

sources.evidence: The government sees no further need for expanding rice cultivation areas in the so-called forest areas

sources.title: Next steps unclear after Indonesia's pledge to stop clearing forests for rice fields
sources.evidence: We will not embark on extensification (clearing) of arable areas.

items.headline: Indonesia reports 7 GW nuclear target in national energy master plan
items.summary: Climate and energy envoy Hashim Djojohadikusumo said on 6 October that a 7 gigawatt nuclear capacity target is included in the national energy master plan, alongside a 100 GWp solar target. An economic ministry official said sites should be chosen by 2026 or 2027 and offers from US, South Korean, Japanese and Russian providers are being evaluated.
items.note: Targets and plans, not approved projects. Statements by government officials.

sources.title: Indonesia targets 7 GW nuclear power capacity for energy security
sources.evidence: Indonesia is targeting the construction of 7 gigawatts (GW) of nuclear power capacity.

items.headline: Sovereign fund Danantara invests US$250 million in US oil producer HighPeak Energy
items.summary: Danantara Indonesia announced on 6 October a US$250 million investment in Texas-based HighPeak Energy through staged convertible preferred stock. The Jakarta Post reported that a listed Indonesian company, Energi Mega Persada, separately invested US$200 million. HighPeak is to develop training programmes for Indonesian workers.
items.note: The US$200 million from Energi Mega Persada is reported by The Jakarta Post only.

sources.title: Indonesia's Danantara invests US$250 million in US oil firm HighPeak
sources.evidence: The transaction is being executed through the issuance of convertible preferred stock across multiple tranches.
